handbook.powerfactor.chips.text:
Electronics start as silicon. Roll silicon into wafers in the Rolling Mill. The Laser Engraver patterns a wafer through a photomask: the mask in its tool slot decides the chip. It isn't used up, but every die wears it a little.

Logic mask + 2 gold nuggets: Microprocessor. Memory mask + 2 redstone: 2 Memory Chips. Power mask + copper dust: 2 Power Transistors. Sensor mask + quartz: Sensor Chip.

Advanced Circuits now need a microprocessor and memory on a printed circuit board. VFD upgrades use power transistors, the clamp meter a sensor chip, the Upgrade Table a microprocessor.
handbook.powerfactor.chips.title: Chips
handbook.powerfactor.devices.text:
Tesla Coil: charges a capacitor from the grid, then throws lightning at the nearest hostile mob it can see within 14 blocks, arcing on to a second one. It never targets players. Each strike costs 2,500 FE and is a sharp reactive pulse on the grid, so give it a strong grid or a capacitor bank nearby, or the lights will flicker.

LED Grow Lamp: hang it above crops. It lights them, so they grow underground, and gives every plant in a 9x9 area up to six blocks below many extra growth ticks: several times faster farms for 24 FE/t.
handbook.powerfactor.devices.title: Tesla Coil & Grow Lamp
handbook.powerfactor.ender.text:
Ender Transmitters turn FE into an EE carrier and beam it to Ender Receivers on the same channel, even across dimensions. The receiver rectifies it back to FE at 85%.

There's a catch. Sending makes the transmitter a big reactive load on its own grid, and busy links radiate interference: every grid within about 48 blocks sees flickering voltage and jittering frequency, so motors slow and trip. Keep wireless away from your factory, or support those grids with capacitors and condensers.
handbook.powerfactor.ender.title: Ender Energy
handbook.powerfactor.generators.text:
Coal Turbine and Diesel Generator: synchronous, so they supply EE. The diesel starts in two seconds and burns modded diesel or fuel, or lava at a worse rate. Hydro Turbine: flowing water around it; also synchronous. Solar Panel and Wind Turbine: FE only.

Wind Turbine: stack Wind Turbine Tower sections (they taper as they rise) and put the turbine on top. The 13-block rotor needs clear air in front, so build at least 6 sections high; taller towers catch stronger wind. It starts at 3 m/s, reaches full output at 12 m/s and pitches its blades to hold it there. Above 25 m/s, in a storm, it feathers and brakes until the wind drops. Cable it at the foot of the tower.

Synchronous Condenser: a spinning machine that only makes EE. Battery Bank: stores 2M FE and automatically holds the grid up when frequency or voltage sags.

Steam power: form a 3x3x3 Steam Boiler with 23 Boiler Casings, one Firebox and two Steam Drums. Feed cold water and furnace fuel through its controller or formed ports. Once hot it produces up to 80 mB/t of steam. Steam Pipes carry only steam, up to 4000 mB per extraction every ten ticks; sneak-use an endpoint to extract, as with fluid pipes. The 3x2x5 Steam Turbine needs 26 Turbine Casings, two Steam Rotors and a Generator Magnet. It synchronizes over ten seconds and generates up to 800 FE/t, with EE support. Use the hologram or sneak-use assembly for either structure. Hot condensate must leave the turbine: pipe it through a powered Cooling Tower, then return its cold water to the boiler. Cooling towers need an open vent to the sky. Steam pipes and turbines accept c:steam from other mods; cooling towers accept c:hot_water. The boiler pauses its burner at 60% pressure and resumes at 40%; blocked outlets hold safely. Dry firing can trip it: supply water and let it cool.

Geothermal Generator: any adjacent lava gives 64 FE/t; magma gives 24. Thermoelectric Generator: put a hot source and water or ice on opposite faces, for up to 48 FE/t. A Rain Collector catches 2 mB/t of actual rain, or 6 during thunderstorms, without FE. A roof stops collection. Pipe its water into your boiler to replenish the loop.
handbook.powerfactor.generators.title: Generators & Storage
handbook.powerfactor.grid.text:
Connected wire of one kind forms a grid, solved every tick like a real AC bus.

Voltage sags as the grid loads up, and EE sags it three times harder than FE. Line loss goes with current squared, and current follows CE, so a poor power factor wastes FE as heat in the wires.

Turbines set the frequency and droop slightly under load (60 Hz down to about 58). They also supply the grid's EE. Solar, wind and batteries can't, so a grid of those plus motors needs capacitors or a synchronous condenser.
handbook.powerfactor.grid.title: Wires and Grids
handbook.powerfactor.hydrogen.text:
Wind blows when it likes. Store it as hydrogen.

The Electrolyzer splits water into hydrogen with grid power (100 FE per 4 mB). Pipe water in and hydrogen out to a Fluid Tank, where it shows as a gas that thickens with pressure.

The Hydrogen Fuel Cell turns it back into FE (about 11 FE per mB, so roughly 45% round trip, like real systems). Its inverter is grid-forming: it sets 60 Hz and supplies EE like a synchronous generator, so wind plus hydrogen can run a whole grid with nothing spinning. The fuel cell also accepts other mods' fluids tagged c:hydrogen.
handbook.powerfactor.hydrogen.title: Hydrogen
handbook.powerfactor.logistics.text:
Item Pipes and Fluid Pipes link up automatically. Arms into inventories insert by default. Right-click an arm with an empty hand to make it extract (orange rings); right-click again to disable it.

Fluid Tanks hold 32 buckets and keep their contents when broken. The Electric Pump draws water from a source block below it without using it up.
handbook.powerfactor.logistics.title: Pipes and Tanks
handbook.powerfactor.machines.text:
Crusher: ore to two dusts, plus gravel, sand and more. Electric Furnace: smelts 25% faster on resistive elements, PF 1.0. Alloy Furnace: induction heating (PF 0.6), makes brass, bronze, electrum and rubber. Arc Furnace: steel, aluminum, silicon and graphite; it needs graphite electrodes and its arc makes the grid flicker. Wire Drawer, Rolling Mill: fine wire and plates. Ore Washer: three dusts per ore with water.

Motor-driven machines slow down on low voltage or frequency and trip below 0.75 pu.

Mechanical Press: fit a Plate Press Die for ingots to plates, or a Gear Press Die for four ingots to a gear. Dies wear once per job and last 512 jobs. Mixer: copper and zinc dust to brass, copper and tin to bronze, or gold and silver to electrum; smelt the blended dust into ingots. Centrifuge: four dirt to a clay ball and sand, or four gravel to flint and two sand. Sawmill: a log to six planks and a stick. All four accept upgrades and side configuration, and support automatic input and output.

Early workshop: craft a Forge Hammer and Wire Cutters from iron and sticks. Two ingots plus a hammer make one plate; a plate plus cutters makes two wires. Both tools return to the grid and wear once per operation. Machines improve material yield: the Rolling Mill or Mechanical Press makes a plate from one ingot, and the Wire Drawer makes three fine wires from one ingot. Heat four coal dust in the Alloy Furnace to make starting graphite for electrodes. The first Arc Furnace uses iron plates and a control circuit, so its own steel and silicon are not needed to build it.

Mix a slimeball, clay ball and coal or charcoal to make two rubber. Natural latex remains renewable. Rubber from other mods can substitute in tagged insulation recipes. Wind turbines now need three blades, two motors, a generator magnet, two steel blocks and an advanced circuit; tower sections craft in pairs.
handbook.powerfactor.machines.title: Machines
handbook.powerfactor.oil.text:
Crude oil lies in reservoirs deep underground, and sometimes seeps up as tar pits in deserts and badlands. Build a Pumpjack above a 3x3 layer of nine Pumpjack Foundation blocks, over a reservoir (it searches straight down, then up to 8 blocks sideways): the nodding donkey lifts 25 mB of crude per tick for 60 FE/t until the reservoir runs dry.

Pipe the crude to an Oil Refinery, a multiblock: the controller sits front-centre of a 3x3 base of Refinery Casing, with three Distillation Column blocks stacked on the middle casing; a hologram shows what's missing. Sneak-use the controller with an empty hand or a structure part to build from inventory. The wind turbine can build its six tower sections the same way. Clear the hologram first; assembly never replaces obstructions. Cables and pipes attach to any casing. The distillation column splits 10 mB of crude into 5 mB of diesel and 4 mB of jet fuel every tick (100 FE/t). Diesel runs the Diesel Generator; jet fuel is available for future aircraft. Buckets work for all three. The refinery accepts other mods' fluids tagged c:crude_oil.
handbook.powerfactor.oil.title: Oil
handbook.powerfactor.ores.text:
New ores: zinc, tin, lead, silver and bauxite (aluminum). Each can be turned off in the common config if another mod provides it. PowerFactor uses the shared c: tags, so other mods' ores work in every machine.

Smelting gives one ingot per ore, the crusher two dusts, and the ore washer three. Alloys: brass (3 copper + zinc), bronze (3 copper + tin), electrum (gold + silver). Steel and aluminum come from the arc furnace.

Rubber trees grow in jungles, swamps and forests. Tap weeping logs with a Tree Tap for latex, then smelt or alloy it into rubber.

Factory construction: Steel Beams form columns and girders (place against a face to choose their axis). Steel Catwalks are thin grated floors. Riveted Steel, Hazard Blocks and Warning Blocks finish walls and mark dangerous machinery. Find their crafting recipes in JEI.
handbook.powerfactor.ores.title: Ores and Materials
handbook.powerfactor.power_factor.text:
Motors draw EE, and lightly loaded motors draw it worst: a crusher idling between jobs runs at about PF 0.25.

Capacitor Banks supply EE locally so the generator doesn't have to, which brings voltage back up and cuts losses. Their output goes with V^2, and too many push the grid to a leading PF and raise the voltage. Above 1.12 pu they trip out.

The Automatic Capacitor Bank switches six 20 EE steps in and out every two seconds to hold the grid near PF 1.0. Watch its cans light up.
handbook.powerfactor.power_factor.title: PF Correction
handbook.powerfactor.power_tools.text:
Electric Chainsaw: an axe on FE. Cut one log of a tree and the whole tree comes down, and its leaves drop their saplings soon after. Sneak to cut a single log. It only fells real trees (logs with natural leaves), so your log cabin is safe.

Electric Jetpack: wear it in the chest slot. Hold Jump to climb; press J by default to toggle hover, which holds you in the air while you build. Sneak to sink. Thrust costs 50 FE/t, hover 18.

Clamp Meter: hold it and look at any wire or machine for a live reading of voltage, frequency, FE, EE, CE and power factor, with a phasor diagram.

Induction Charging Pad: stand on it and everything you carry charges.

Power Armor: helmet, chest plate, exoskeleton leggings and boots have individual FE batteries. Charge them in a Charger or by standing on a powered Charging Pad. The hull supplies iron-level armor without power. Each charged piece shields 8% of damage remaining after armor, paying 120 FE per point absorbed; Plating adds 2% per module, capped at 50% for the suit. Leg servos add 25% movement speed, higher jumps and one-block steps. Speed modules add 15% each; Jump Servo modules add height. Sneak or disable movement assists to move normally. Boots spend FE to cushion five blocks of a fall beyond the safe distance; Shock Absorbers add three blocks each. Empty batteries stop powered abilities. Open suit settings with B to see batteries and toggle movement assists, night vision or jetpack hover.

Put a chest plate in the Upgrade Table and fit an actual Electric Jetpack into a socket. It remains removable with its stored charge and upgrades; flight uses the chest battery. Thruster and Efficiency modules in the chest and fitted jetpack combine up to the usual three-module limit. Hold Jump to climb, J toggles hover by default and Sneak descends. All armor takes Battery, Efficiency and Plating modules. Helmets also take Night Vision and Rebreather modules for powered vision and underwater air. The helmet utilities, locomotion, landing cushion and shield all consume FE; keep an eye on the four-battery HUD.

Movement kit: the Powered Grapple has a 64-block cable and 120,000 FE battery. G casts or retracts from your inventory; right-click works when held. The hook attaches to solid terrain or a moving entity. It reels you toward the anchor for 12 FE/t; hold Sneak to stop the reel and swing on a fixed cable. Jump releases without killing momentum. Broken anchors, obstructed cables, excessive range, empty batteries or dropping the device release the hook. Fit Battery, Efficiency or Speed modules in the Upgrade Table to improve the grapple.

A Wingsuit can be worn directly or fitted into a Power Chestplate socket alongside a jetpack. Press U in the air to deploy or fold. Look down to dive for speed; look up to trade speed for lift. A/D bank and Sneak airbrakes. Low airspeed stalls: the wingsuit needs altitude and momentum. Release a swinging or reeling grapple into a glide to keep your speed. A fitted jetpack can regain altitude: Jump folds the wingsuit and resumes thrust. Wingsuit fabric folds smoothly, stretches between the arms and hips, and has a leg membrane. Its gliding pose, camera bank and wind sound follow motion. The suit screen controls both flight modes, and the movement HUD shows cable mode, charge, distance and airspeed.

The Electric Rover is a fast single-seat off-road vehicle with a 500,000 FE battery. Place it on clear ground and right-click to sit. W/S accelerate and reverse, A/D steer, Jump brakes and Sprint boosts. Sneak exits. It climbs one-block steps using collision handling, and brakes automatically if the driver leaves or input stops. Drive uses 20 FE/t, boost 50 FE/t. Empty batteries coast but cannot accelerate. Park above a powered Charging Pad to recharge; the packed vehicle also charges as an FE item. Sneak-use a wrench on a stopped, empty rover to pack it without losing battery or hull state. Steel ingots repair 10 HP each. The chassis has 80 HP; a destroyed rover becomes scrap.
handbook.powerfactor.power_tools.title: Power Tools
handbook.powerfactor.radio.text: Walkie-talkies use your real microphone through the Simple Voice Chat mod. Hold one and talk: everyone carrying a switched-on walkie-talkie on the same channel hears you through its little speaker, with more static the further away they are, out to about 190 blocks. Use the walkie-talkie to change channel (1-16); sneak-use to switch it off. Talking uses a little charge; charge it in a charger.\n\nRadio Towers relay calls: when both people are within about 96 blocks of a powered tower, they can talk at any distance, crystal clear. A blackout takes the towers off the air.
handbook.powerfactor.radio.title: Radio
handbook.powerfactor.scada.text:
SCADA is the control room. Run Fiber Optic Cable from a SCADA Terminal to your machines: it lists every device live with ON/OFF switches, system totals and 60-second frequency and voltage trends. Alarms sound on faults.

SCADA Displays placed side by side form one wall screen that lays itself out by size, from a single readout up to a full HMI with an automatic one-line diagram of your grid. Connect any panel to fiber; right-click to change page.
handbook.powerfactor.scada.title: SCADA
handbook.powerfactor.start.text:
Welcome to PowerFactor: AC power the way real grids work.

Build a Coal Turbine (iron, copper coils, turbine blades, a furnace) and feed it coal. It takes about ten seconds to spin up to 3,600 RPM. Its breaker closes at 57 Hz and it starts pushing FE out of every face except the front. Run Copper Wire from it to your machines.

Right-click any machine for its GUI. The tabs on the right edge hold the Electrical analyzer, Upgrades and Configuration.
handbook.powerfactor.start.title: Getting Started
handbook.powerfactor.title: PowerFactor
handbook.powerfactor.tools.text:
Electric Drill: pickaxe and shovel on FE. Sneak-use to install modules: 3x3 Area, Speed, Silk Touch, Fortune, Magnet, Battery.

Tesla Arc Gun: lightning that arcs between up to five targets.

Arc Saber: use to ignite, sneak-use to pick any RGB color, blade style (solid, plasma, crackling arc, rainbow) and hit effect (stun, ignite, chain arc, drain). Charge everything in a Charger.
handbook.powerfactor.tools.title: Tools and Weapons
handbook.powerfactor.transmission.text:
Low voltage loses a lot over distance. Step up.

Wire tiers: Copper Wire (512 CE), Insulated Cable (1,024), MV Aluminum Cable (4,096), and HV pylons (16,384) with far lower loss. Bare and insulated copper share 480 V and connect directly; a mixed run uses its weakest cable's rating. Different voltages need a transformer, including across closed breaker chains. Transformers join two grids: power enters the red primary face and leaves the blue secondary face, and they carry EE back upstream. Overload one and it trips; right-click to reset.

String HV conductors between pylons with a Conductor Spool, up to 32 blocks per span. Circuit Breakers split a grid when open and trip on overcurrent.
handbook.powerfactor.transmission.title: Transmission
handbook.powerfactor.units.text:
PowerFactor measures three kinds of power.

FE (Forge Energy) is real power: it does the work, and every FE machine from any mod runs on it.

EE (Ender Energy) is reactive power. Motors need it to magnetize, but it does no work. It still has to be generated and carried.

CE (Creative Energy) is apparent power, the total the wires and generators actually see: CE = sqrt(FE^2 + EE^2).

Power factor is FE / CE. At 1.00 every bit of capacity does work.
handbook.powerfactor.units.title: FE, EE and CE
handbook.powerfactor.upgrades.text:
Upgrades go in the Upgrades tab.

Speed: +50% per card, but a bigger motor uses more FE and EE. Efficiency: -15% FE per job. Built-in Capacitor: cancels 5 EE of the machine's own motor each; three fix a stock crusher. VFD: the motor ignores frequency and voltage sag, uses a quarter of the EE and stops instead of idling. Surge Protector: rides through dips down to 0.6 pu. Capacity: a bigger FE buffer.

The Configuration tab sets redstone behavior, each face's role (input, output, both, closed) and auto-input and auto-eject.
handbook.powerfactor.upgrades.title: Upgrade Cards
handbook.powerfactor.upgrades_tools.text:
Put a Drill, Chainsaw, Jetpack, Arc Saber or Arc Gun in the middle of an Upgrade Table and fit up to six modules round it. Battery and Efficiency fit everything. Speed and Magnet suit the drill and chainsaw; Area, Silk Touch and Fortune the drill; Thruster and Plating the jetpack; Overcharge the blades and the gun; Chain Arc the saber and gun. Sockets light up for modules that fit. Modules travel inside the tool.

Wrench: turns machines, strips wire coating, and sneak-use dismantles any PowerFactor block into your inventory.
handbook.powerfactor.wire_safety.text: Bare wire on a live grid shocks whatever touches it: copper (480 V) stings, bare MV aluminium (13.8 kV) throws you back hard. Right-click a wire with Rubber to coat it; coated and insulated cable are safe to walk on. A wrench strips the coat off again. Mobs that wander onto bare live wire get the same treatment.
